title: The Safehouse of the Free Port
premise: Wren Blackwood, a disgraced intelligence analyst hiding in a free-port safehouse in Hamburg after the 'incident' that burned his last agency, discovers the property has been listed online with interior photos — including the wall of documents he was never supposed to photograph. The listing is bait: someone from his past knows what he kept hidden there, a ledger proving his former handler sold state secrets through the port's bonded warehouses. As buyers, brokers, and killers converge before Frankfurt markets open Monday, Wren must decide whether to sell the ledger to the highest bidder or expose it. In the end he leaks it publicly at dawn, sacrificing his own anonymity and any chance of restoration — but freeing himself from the secret that has kept him sleepless.
about_author: Yara Sterling is the pen name of a former financial-crimes investigator who spent a decade inside Europe's free ports before trading her clearance for fiction. She writes thrillers about people who know too much and trust too little, drawing on the gray economies she once audited.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Scrolling auction listings at 3 a.m., Wren finds his safehouse photographed room by room — including the sealed storeroom holding the Halvorsen ledger. A viewing is scheduled for Sunday; the agent's name belongs to a woman he buried in a file six years ago. Emotional beat: cold dread hardening into purpose as invisibility dies and Wren chooses to stop running.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Wren and Ilse Varga, the ex-handler's fixer posing as estate agent. At the staged open house, three bidders circle: a Frankfurt fund manager, a port authority insider, and a quiet man Wren recognizes as the incident's surviving witness. Ilse offers Wren a clean exit if he hands over the ledger by midnight. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into clarity — everyone wants the same thing, and only one of them can leave with it.

chapters.title: Bonded
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Trapped inside the free port after hours when the sale closes early and the exits seal, Wren races to copy and distribute the ledger while the quiet man hunts him through the warehouse maze. He learns the incident wasn't his failure but his handler's cover-up, engineered to discredit him. Emotional beat: rage and grief fusing into resolve as betrayal becomes proof.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, then brief coda from Ilse. At 7 a.m., minutes before Frankfurt opens, Wren uploads the ledger to every wire service at once and walks out of the port unarmed, surrendering to the first police car he sees. Markets wobble; arrests follow within hours. Ilse burns the listing and disappears. Emotional beat: exhausted peace — Wren finally sleeps, not because he's safe, but because he's no longer hiding.
